evidence: Assess usable length and width - not just litres

evidence: They spend the day in the protection of Pandanus roots or other structures, and feed at night. It is normally seen alone or in small groups.
sourceTypeNeeded: Source describing activity pattern and territoriality
uncertainty: Wild activity pattern; captive lighting may shift feeding to daytime, which is unverified here.

evidence: Asian arowanas are carnivorous and should be fed a high-quality diet of meaty food, such as shrimp and crickets.
sourceTypeNeeded: Source describing captive diet and feeding position
uncertainty: No feeding frequency sourced; the page's list of accepted foods is long (mealworms, earthworms, feeder fish, lean pork, pelleted food) but some entries come from aquarist advice rather than peer review.

evidence: Keep singly or with large tankmates, since they are predatory and territorial
sourceTypeNeeded: Source stating tankmate rules for the species
uncertainty: No named species lists were sourced; do not generate compatible/incompatible species lists from this evidence (relation destinations are out of scope for Stage A).

evidence: S. formosus is one of only eight fish species listed on Appendix I.
sourceTypeNeeded: Sources covering legal status, enclosure scale and behaviour
uncertainty: Legal details vary by country and change over time; cite the CITES/IUCN position as of the checked date and link keepers to their local authority. TankBud additionally warns: 'Do not release aquarium specimens into local waterways.'

evidence: Aquarium base 180 x 60cm - ~648 litres - absolute bare minimum for an adult fish though the bigger the tank the better.
sourceTypeNeeded: Aquarium husbandry profile giving explicit tank dimensions for adult S. jardinii
uncertainty: Only one fetched source states dimensions; TankBud gives a larger 1,200 L minimum without dimensions. 180 cm is the explicit published floor, not a ceiling.

evidence: Aquarium base 180 x 60cm - ~648 litres - absolute bare minimum for an adult fish
sourceTypeNeeded: Aquarium husbandry profile giving explicit tank dimensions for adult S. jardinii
uncertainty: Width comes from the same single profile; no second source gives a width figure. TankBud only gives volume (1,200 L).

evidence: This species requires a lot of swimming space and decor is not really critical.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source explicitly describing swimming-space needs
uncertainty: Not quantified beyond the 180 x 60 cm base; HIGH is derived from a 90-100 cm adult that must use the full length of the tank.

evidence: Needs a tight-fitting lid as this species is known to jump. The tank should also have a very heavy, tightly fitting cover, as the fish are powerful jumpers.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source stating this species jumps and how to contain it
uncertainty: Direct husbandry statement; no fetched source quantifies jump height, so do not publish a number. TankBud independently says saratogas jump hard.

evidence: Needs a tight-fitting lid as this species is known to jump. The tank should also have a very heavy, tightly fitting cover, as the fish are powerful jumpers.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source stating the cover requirement for this species
uncertainty: Single-source requirement, corroborated in substance by TankBud ('a heavy, tight lid, since saratogas jump hard'). Airmesh tops that flex are not covered by the sources - heavy and tight are the stated words.

evidence: Usually found in slow-moving or still bodies of water, including streams, creeks, billabongs and swamps. Tends to prefer areas of clear water, where there is some surface vegetation or overhanging branches.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source describing preferred water movement for the species
uncertainty: Habitat-derived: the same profile demands strong, efficient filtration, so filter output must be aimed away from the surface hunting lane rather than reduced.

evidence: The species is an air-gulper adapted to warm, oxygen-poor billabongs.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source documenting air breathing or low-oxygen tolerance
uncertainty: Air gulping is documented but no fetched source quantifies dissolved-oxygen tolerance; do not publish a ppm figure. Surface access is the real constraint.

evidence: Filtration needs to be strong and efficient, as if the fish are kept in sub-standard conditions for prolonged periods they can develop problems with their eyes and gills. Regular water changes must be strictly observed for the same reason.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source stating filtration and water-quality expectations for the species
uncertainty: The source never uses the word cycled; maturity is inferred from the documented consequences of prolonged sub-standard water quality (eye and gill problems).

evidence: Filtration needs to be strong and efficient... at ~648 litres and a turnover of four to five times the volume an hour, look for two filters rated 1295-1620 lph each.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source describing filtration capacity for the species
uncertainty: Waste output is not quantified; HIGH is inferred from a 90-100 cm carnivore plus the explicit four-to-five-times-per-hour turnover recommendation.

evidence: Regular water changes must be strictly observed for the same reason. [eye and gill problems in sub-standard conditions]
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source giving explicit water-change or water-quality guidance
uncertainty: No percentage or schedule is given by any fetched source; do not invent one. The consequence (eye and gill problems) is explicit.

evidence: Adults occur in still waters of streams and swamps where it is usually seen near the surface or close to shore among aquatic vegetation. Solitary, territorial.
sourceTypeNeeded: Sources describing swim position and social behaviour
uncertainty: Surface-oriented and shore/structure-associated rather than open-pelagic; the open_water_swimmer flag is recorded as surface orientation, backed by Seriously Fish's statement that it requires a lot of swimming space.

evidence: Solitary, territorial and spawn prior to the wet season when surface water temperatures approach 30°C.
sourceTypeNeeded: Sources stating social behaviour / group size
uncertainty: Seriously Fish notes 6-10 adults can be housed together only in a tank large enough to disperse fighting, which it says almost nobody has; single housing is its stated general rule.

evidence: Will eat smaller fish but is suitable for some communities of larger species, although some individuals won't tolerate any tankmates whatsoever. Most specimens are very territorial and belligerent towards other arowana.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry source describing tankmate tolerance for the species
uncertainty: Individual variation is explicitly documented - no tankmate combination is guaranteed. Seriously Fish suggests large catfish, characins, cyprinids, knifefish and robust cichlids as candidates, added last and watched.

evidence: Will eat smaller fish but is suitable for some communities of larger species.
sourceTypeNeeded: Source documenting predation on smaller fish
uncertainty: No source gives a size threshold; the practical rule is anything that fits in the mouth, corroborated by FishBase documenting small fishes in the wild diet.

evidence: It is widely considered the most aggressive arowana in aquaria, and some individuals will not tolerate any tankmates. [TankBud: Temperament Aggressive]
sourceTypeNeeded: Two independent sources describing temperament of this species
uncertainty: Corroborated by TankBud (Temperament: Aggressive; Adults are territorial and often aggressive toward their own kind) and FishBase (solitary, territorial). Seriously Fish's own temperament badge reads predatory.

evidence: Primarily a surface feeder, feeding on a variety of terrestrial and aquatic insects, small fishes, frogs, crustaceans, and some plant material.
sourceTypeNeeded: Source documenting natural diet including invertebrates
uncertainty: Aquarium-specific invertebrate-predation reports were not located, but crustaceans and insects are routine wild prey.

evidence: Volume ~648 litres - 180 x 60 x 60 cm - absolute bare minimum for an adult fish though the bigger the tank the better.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry profile stating an adult volume minimum for the species
uncertainty: TankBud states a larger 1,200 L minimum; 648 L is the lower published floor from the source that also gives dimensions. Single-source figures - treat 648 L as the floor and 1,200 L as the recommendation.

evidence: Hardness: 8-15°H

uncertainty: Single source; FishBase does not publish a dH range for this species and the profile's own quick-facts badge says hardness not recorded.

evidence: Hardness: 8-15°H

evidence: Asia and Oceania: northern Australia and central-southern New Guinea. Adults occur in still waters of streams and swamps where it is usually seen near the surface or close to shore among aquatic vegetation. IUCN Least Concern; CITES Not Evaluated.
sourceTypeNeeded: Database or institutional species account covering distribution and habitat
uncertainty: IUCN assessment dates from February 2019. Trade names (pearl arowana, Jardini arowana, Gulf saratoga) are market labels for the same species; TankBud's claim that the male mouthbroods conflicts with FishBase and Seriously Fish, both of which state the female carries the brood - do not repeat TankBud's version.

evidence: Maturity: Lm 45.0. Max length: 100.0 cm SL. Common length: 55.0 cm SL. [Seriously Fish: Length 900mm SL; TankBud: adult size 90 cm]

uncertainty: Growth rate per year was not found in any fetched source. Maximum length rests on one FishBase reference; Seriously Fish (90 cm) and TankBud (90 cm) are slightly more conservative.

evidence: 180 x 60 x 60 cm - ~648 litres - absolute bare minimum for an adult fish... The tank should also have a very heavy, tightly fitting cover, as the fish are powerful jumpers. Filtration needs to be strong and efficient.
sourceTypeNeeded: Husbandry profile stating tank scale and cover requirements
uncertainty: Published floor is single-source (Seriously Fish 648 L); TankBud asks for 1,200 L. Water parameters are not restated here because sources disagree marginally (Seriously Fish 24-29 C and pH 6.8-7.5 vs profile 24-30 C and 6-7.5) - no material correction.

evidence: Aquarium base 180 x 60cm... This species requires a lot of swimming space and decor is not really critical.

evidence: Most specimens are very territorial and belligerent towards other arowana, unless you have enough space to comfortably house 6-10 individuals... as a general rule this species should be kept singly. [FishBase: Solitary, territorial]
sourceTypeNeeded: Sources describing social behaviour and territoriality
uncertainty: The 6-10 group figure is explicitly conditional on space almost no aquarist has; no fetched source describes temperament towards non-arowana tankmates as reliable.

evidence: Better alternatives include earthworms, gut-loaded mealworms, waxworms, and frozen and dried foods such as bloodworm, prawn (leave the shells on), mussel and pellets. Try to keep the diet varied, or the fish may become addicted to a particular type of food.

uncertainty: The 12-inch switch from several small feedings to one feeding per day is Seriously Fish's own guidance and is not independently corroborated; live feeder fish are advised against, not banned.

evidence: Will eat smaller fish but is suitable for some communities of larger species, although some individuals won't tolerate any tankmates whatsoever. uncertainty: The candidate tankmate list is one source's suggestion with explicit individual variation; no combination is guaranteed and smaller fish are always at risk as the arowana grows.

uncertainty: Verdict rests on one comprehensive hobbyist profile plus TankBud's larger 1,200 L figure; no institutional husbandry manual was located for this species.
